doc.headline: No configuration is shown to pass both gates: only two, Atlas-M and Brisk-S with high reasoning and retry, hold {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} in every task, and both run over the {criteria.p95.threshold} latency budget.
doc.lede: Multi-hop lookups are every configuration's weakest task; the configuration that comes closest inside the budget, Brisk-S with low reasoning and retry, falls short there by {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.multihop.gap|abs} points. Per-task latency, never recorded, could open a routed mix nobody has run.

caveats.material_if: Only for a claim that one configuration beats another: the call reads each configuration against the declared gates.

Only where a configuration clears a gate by little. Brisk-S with high reasoning and retry clears multi-hop by {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.multihop.gap} points, best of {n_candidates|words}; a fresh run would likely read it lower. That strengthens the headline but weakens the fallback and the routed mix, both of which lean on its thin clearances.

caveats.label: Task pass rates state no case count
caveats.material_if: If the true per-task rates of the two Brisk-S configurations with retry sit on the other side of the gate from today's readings. High reasoning would lose the fallback if its multi-hop or ambiguous-entity pass flipped. Low reasoning would become a single-configuration candidate only if both its misses flipped, multi-hop and ambiguous entities, and its date math, exactly on the line, held.

caveats.label: Latency recorded only over all cases
caveats.material_if: Only for a routed mix nobody ran: if each configuration's tail latency stays inside the budget in the tasks it would serve, the mix could clear both gates. It cannot rescue a single high-reasoning configuration, whose tail over all cases is already over budget.

decision.text: On multi-hop lookups the two gates pull against each other: only high reasoning with retry reaches {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} there, and both such passers run over {criteria.p95.threshold} on tail latency. Ship none under the gates as declared.

If every case belongs to exactly one task, neither pass-rate passer can meet the latency gate on its own, since each one's tail over all cases is over budget. On today's readings every configuration inside the budget misses multi-hop, the nearest by {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.multihop.gap|abs} points, a miss not yet settled.

The Brisk-S readings nearest the gate are all thin and carry no case count. If each task held its traffic share of cases, a run of today's size would read high reasoning's multi-hop pass below the line {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.task.multihop.wrong_side} of the time and its ambiguous-entity pass {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.task.disamb.wrong_side}; it would read low reasoning's multi-hop miss above the line {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.task.multihop.wrong_side} and its ambiguous-entity miss {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.task.disamb.wrong_side}. Low reasoning's date math sits exactly on the line.

Per-task tail latency for a routed mix: Brisk-S with high reasoning and retry on multi-hop and ambiguous-entity lookups ({task.multihop.share} and {task.disamb.share} of traffic), Brisk-S with low reasoning and retry on single lookups and date math. Its legs also need their thin pass rates settled. If the mix fails, the planner's owner has to say which gate gives way on multi-hop.

claims.text: Only {count.passing.pass_rate|words} of the {n_candidates|words} configurations reach {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} in every task, Atlas-M and Brisk-S with high reasoning and retry; multi-hop lookups are the weakest task for every configuration.

evidence.caption: Pass rate by task and configuration; cells under the {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} gate are outlined.

claims.text: Both run over the latency budget on tail latency across all cases: {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.high.r1.p95} for Brisk-S and {measure.latency_ms.atlas-m.high.r1.p95} for Atlas-M, against {criteria.p95.threshold}. Latency was kept only over all cases, so the per-task gate has no figure; but if every case belongs to exactly one task, each must miss the budget in some task, so per-task latency can rescue only a routed mix, not either configuration alone.

evidence.caption: Median to tail latency ({criteria.p95.statistic}) over all cases for each configuration, the {criteria.p95.threshold} budget marked.

claims.text: Brisk-S with retry sits at the gate at both reasoning levels: with low reasoning ({measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r1.p95}) it misses {count.failing.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1|words} tasks, multi-hop by {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.multihop.gap|abs} points and ambiguous entities by {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.disamb.gap|abs}; with high reasoning it clears multi-hop by only {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.multihop.gap} and ambiguous entities by {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.disamb.gap}. With no case counts, neither the misses nor the passes are settled.

evidence.caption: Per-task pass rate for Brisk-S with retry at low and at high reasoning, the gate marked; task rates state no case count, so no interval is drawn.

claims.text: Of the two that hold the pass rate in every task, Atlas-M costs {cost.gap.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.multiple} as much as Brisk-S, {cost.gap.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.monthly|abs} more a month.

evidence.caption: Cost per thousand calls for the two pass-rate passers and the nearest miss inside the budget, on a log scale.

claims.text: The kept multi-hop failure of Brisk-S with low reasoning and retry merges two hops into one search; the date and ambiguous-entity cards fail other ways, an off-by-one window and a missing clarifying question.

evidence.caption: The failures kept for this configuration, one per task where a failure was kept; the input does not say how many failed in all.

explore.binds: Which configurations pass the latency gate in each task
explore.outcome: No budget value changes the call: latency has no per-task figure, so the gate reads nothing at any threshold. Read over all cases instead, a budget at or above {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.high.r1.p95} would admit Brisk-S with high reasoning and retry, subject to its thin multi-hop and ambiguous-entity passes.

explore.binds: Which configurations hold the pass rate in every task
explore.outcome: Lowering it admits more configurations on pass rate, Brisk-S with low reasoning and retry once the gate is lowered to {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.multihop.value}, but no configuration passes both gates while latency has no per-task figure.

As a what-if, if tasks held their traffic share of cases, a run sized to settle most of the time needs {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.task.multihop.cases_needed_two_sided_80} multi-hop and {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.task.disamb.cases_needed_two_sided_80} ambiguous-entity cases.

On the same what-if, settling most of the time needs {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.task.multihop.cases_needed_two_sided_80} multi-hop and {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.task.disamb.cases_needed_two_sided_80} ambiguous-entity cases; date math sits exactly on the line, so no run settles it unless the true rate is away from the line.

method.text: {scoreboard.brisk-s.high.r1.cases} cases per configuration, with no repeats stated. The input does not say how cases split across tasks, only each task's share of traffic: {task.single.share} single lookups, {task.multihop.share} multi-hop, {task.datemath.share} date and unit math, {task.disamb.share} ambiguous entities.
The input does not define what makes a task pass; its failure classes are a missing call, wrong arguments and the wrong tool.

Pass rate at least {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} in each task, and tail latency ({criteria.p95.statistic}) at most {criteria.p95.threshold} in each task, both declared before the run. Latency was recorded only over all cases, so the latency gate has no figure in any task; a configuration with no failing figure is undecided, not failed.

Its pass-rate column is the overall pass rate across all tasks. The gate reads each task, so an overall rate at or above the gate does not mean a configuration passes; read the per-task chart instead.

Run sizes and wrong-side odds for per-task rates read each task as holding its traffic share of a configuration's cases, a what-if because the input states no per-task count; on that reading multi-hop holds {assumed.share.spread.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.task.multihop.n} cases.
Per-task pass rates state no case count and carry no interval. There is no control, so nothing is paired, and no multiplicity correction applies.
Cost per thousand calls as measured. Monthly figures multiply it by the declared volume of {meta.volume_per_month}, and the input does not say what that volume counts.

findings.finding: Next step 4 ('Improve multi-hop planning… where the kept failure merges hops into one search') rests on one kept card, TQ-0418. The snapshot doesn't say how many multi-hop failures there were for Brisk-S with low reasoning and retry, so hop-collapse may not be the main pattern. Fix: make step 4 conditional, e.g. first tally that configuration's multi-hop failures by pattern from the traces, then target planning only if hop-collapse dominates. c-fail could say in its sentence, not only its caption, that this is one example.

items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline, decision block and c-gates make the call clear: ship nothing under the gates as declared. Multi-hop lookups are named as the problem. But 'What would settle it' gives the main way out as a mix that sends only multi-hop lookups to Brisk-S high reasoning with retry. The page's own figures show that mix fails the pass-rate gate on ambiguous entities. 'What we know despite it' also presents Brisk-S high reasoning with retry holding the pass rate as settled, when its multi-hop pass is 0.3 points with no case count behind it.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: c-gates, c-latency and c-nearest each match their own tables. Two things break the thread. First, the routed mix in the lede caveat, the decision block and next step 1 serves every task except multi-hop from a fast configuration. Yet the c-nearest block shows the best fast option, Brisk-S low reasoning with retry, at 96.4% on ambiguous entities, and no configuration under 600 ms overall reaches 97% there. Second, c-lever reads the reasoning step on overall pass rate (+0.8, not separated). The Left-out list itself calls overall pass rate misleading. On multi-hop, the step is +1.7 (95.6% to 97.3%), and that is exactly what takes Brisk-S over the gate.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: The page treats Brisk-S low reasoning with retry's 0.6-point ambiguous-entity miss as noise, which is fair. It treats Brisk-S high reasoning with retry's 0.3-point multi-hop pass as fact ('What we know despite it', next step 4). Neither has a case count. If each task held its traffic share of the 1,200 cases, a same-size run would put the high-reasoning multi-hop reading below the line 37.4% of the time. The low-reasoning ambiguous-entity miss would land above it 33.3% of the time. So the two are about equally unsettled. The best-of-eighteen caveat calls this a strengthening, which is true for the headline, but it weakens the fallback the page recommends.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: None of the omitted items would change the call. The other thin misses belong to configurations whose overall tail latency (810 ms, 2430 ms) already implies a per-task latency failure. Nano-XS reaches the gate in no task. The one inconsistency: overall pass rate is listed as left out, yet c-lever and c-cost both rely on it.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: Latency recorded only over all cases is carried into the story, the Explore table and next step 1. No control is handled correctly. The missing per-task case count, though, is carried only for Brisk-S low reasoning with retry, not for the configuration the fallback rests on. c-latency's inference also depends on the tasks splitting the cases between them, and the page never says so.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each step names a run or a declaration and what it would settle, and the re-run sizes for Brisk-S low reasoning with retry check out (1,685 and 7,567 cases). But next step 1 is built around a multi-hop-only mix that cannot clear the pass-rate gate. No step checks whether Brisk-S high reasoning with retry really clears multi-hop, and next step 4's fallback depends on that.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: c-gates, c-latency and c-nearest each show their claim clearly. c-cost claims a pass-rate gap (-1.7 to +0.4) that its block doesn't draw: it shows only cost. c-fail's caption says 'one per task where it failed', but this configuration also fails 1.6% of single lookups and has no card there. c-lever prints an interval end as '+0.03535'.

findings.finding: The routed mix offered as the way out (lede caveat 'sending only that task to it could clear both gates', 'What would settle it', next step 1) sends only multi-hop lookups to Brisk-S high reasoning with retry. That mix can't pass the pass-rate gate. The other tasks would go to a fast configuration, and none under 600 ms overall reaches 97% on ambiguous entities: the best is Brisk-S low reasoning with retry at 96.4% (c-nearest block). Fix: describe the mix as multi-hop and ambiguous-entity lookups (40% of traffic) on Brisk-S high reasoning with retry, and single lookups and date math on Brisk-S low reasoning with retry. Say that date math sits exactly on the line (97.0%). Ask next step 1 for per-task tail latency on both of those tasks.

'What we know despite it' and next step 4 present Brisk-S high reasoning with retry as holding the pass rate in every task, as if no caveat applied. Its multi-hop reading clears by 0.3 points with no case count, and it was picked from eighteen. If tasks held their traffic share of cases (300 multi-hop), a same-size run would read it under the line 37.4% of the time. Fix: take that statement out of 'despite it'. Apply the no-case-count caveat to this configuration as well as Brisk-S low reasoning with retry. Add a next step that states its multi-hop case count, or re-runs it, and say the fallback depends on that result.

The claim reads the low-to-high reasoning step on overall pass rate (+0.8, -0.4 to +2.1), a figure the page itself says misleads because the gate reads each task. On multi-hop, the step from Brisk-S low to high reasoning with retry is +1.7 (95.6% to 97.3%), and that is what takes it over the gate. Reframe the claim on multi-hop, noting it carries no interval, or explain why the overall effect matters for the call.

The sentence claims Brisk-S's pass rate minus Atlas-M's is not told apart from zero (-1.7 to +0.4), but the block draws only cost. Add the gap (-0.7 overall, with its interval) or the per-task gaps (-0.6 to -0.7 in every task, no interval). Also note this uses overall pass rate, which the page elsewhere sets aside.

State the condition behind 'at least one task's tail is over it too': it holds only if the tasks split the cases between them, with no case in two tasks or none. Then draw the conclusion: both pass-rate passers fail the latency gate in some task, so per-task latency can only rescue a routed mix, not a single configuration. Narrow 'whether any configuration' in 'What would settle it' and next step 1 to match.
The caption 'one per task where it failed' is wrong. Brisk-S low reasoning with retry also fails 1.6% of single lookups (98.4%) and has no card there. Say 'one per task where a failure was kept'.
The retry-at-high-reasoning interval prints as '+0.03535 to +2.6'. Round it to +0.04 so it matches the other rows.

The lede calls Brisk-S low reasoning with retry 'the fastest near miss'. It isn't the fastest: several Nano-XS and Brisk-S configurations are faster. It is the closest to the pass-rate gate within the latency budget, as c-nearest says. Use c-nearest's wording.

items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline, the decision block and c-gates together tell a reader what to do and why. Ship nothing under the gates as declared: only two configurations hold 97% in every task, and both are over 600 ms on tail latency across all cases. The main risk is clear too: multi-hop is where the gates pull against each other, and per-task latency for a routed mix is the open question. The previous round's 'fastest near miss' wording is fixed; the lede now says 'comes closest inside the budget'. Two small issues remain. The headline's 'the two with high reasoning and retry' reads as if there were only two such configurations, but Nano-XS with high reasoning and retry is a third. And the Options table prints overall pass rate, where six configurations show 97% or more.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: The two previous must_fix findings are resolved. The routed mix now sends multi-hop and ambiguous-entity lookups to Brisk-S with high reasoning and retry, and single lookups and date math to Brisk-S with low reasoning and retry. Date math is flagged as sitting on the line. Brisk-S with high reasoning and retry is no longer listed under 'despite it'. c-gates matches its heatmap row by row: multi-hop is the lowest row in every column, and only Atlas-M and Brisk-S with high reasoning and retry pass all four rows. But 'What we know despite it' states as settled that every configuration inside the budget misses multi-hop. That rests on Brisk-S with low reasoning and retry missing by 1.4 points, and c-nearest says 'neither the misses nor the pass are settled'. Next step 3 also asks 'whether its misses are real'. So the page contradicts itself.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: The 0.3-point multi-hop clearance of Brisk-S with high reasoning and retry is now caveated well (37.4% wrong-side under the traffic-share what-if). But the same configuration's other clears are thin too, and the page never says so: ambiguous entity at 97.6% (29.9% wrong-side) and date math at 97.9% (16.5%). Its ambiguous-entity leg carries 15% of traffic in the routed mix. The confidence caveat also says one flip for low reasoning 'would make it a single-configuration candidate'. In fact it would need two flips, multi-hop (1.4 points short, 11.9% wrong-side) and ambiguous entity, plus date math holding exactly on the line.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: Nothing omitted would change the call. Dominance with gates read as gates leaves no survivor. Only Atlas-M and Brisk-S with high reasoning and retry are undecided, and both are over budget across all cases. The thin misses left out (Atlas-M high reasoning without retry, Brisk-S high reasoning without retry) are on configurations over budget across all cases. Overall pass rate is rightly set aside, though it still appears in the Options table.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: The missing per-task latency is carried into the headline, into c-latency (with the partition condition now stated, as asked last round) and into next step 1. The missing case counts and the pick being best of eighteen are carried into Watch and into the re-run steps. 'No control' is correctly marked as not bearing on a gate-based call.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each step names an experiment or a declaration and says what it settles. Step 1 now asks for per-task latency on both legs of the mix, as asked last round. Steps 2 and 3 give run sizes that match the tool (22,911 multi-hop cases; 1,685 multi-hop and 7,567 ambiguous-entity cases). Step 5 names who decides which gate gives way. One gap: step 2 re-runs Brisk-S with high reasoning and retry on multi-hop only, though the mix also relies on its thin ambiguous-entity pass.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: c-gates' heatmap shows the gate per cell. c-latency's bars show 870 ms and 2551 ms against the 600 ms line. c-nearest draws both Brisk-S configurations with retry against the gate, with the gaps readable (95.6, 96.4, 97.3, 97.0). c-cost's bars hold $3.48 and $0.63 (5.5 times, and $11,376 a month at 4,000,000, which checks). c-fail's cards match the examples exactly, and its caption is fixed. c-cost's 'runs further over the latency budget' is not drawn in its block, but c-latency shows it.

findings.finding: 'What we know despite it' states as known that every configuration inside the budget misses the pass-rate gate on multi-hop. The closest one, Brisk-S with low reasoning and retry, misses by 1.4 points (95.6%) with no case count. c-nearest says 'neither the misses nor the pass are settled', and next step 3 re-runs it to learn 'whether its misses are real'. If tasks held their traffic share of cases (300 multi-hop), a same-size run would read that miss on the other side of the line 11.9% of the time. Fix: qualify the statement ('on today's readings; the nearest miss, 1.4 points, is not settled'), or move it out of 'despite it'. Add the 11.9% to Watch next to the 37.4% and 33.3%.

The confidence caveat on case counts says 'a flip for low reasoning would make it a single-configuration candidate', and pairs only its ambiguous-entity miss with high reasoning's multi-hop pass. Brisk-S with low reasoning and retry also misses multi-hop (95.6%) and sits exactly on the line in date math (97.0%). It would become a candidate only if both misses flipped and date math held. Fix: say that, and name the multi-hop miss alongside the ambiguous-entity miss.

The page treats the 0.3-point multi-hop clearance as the only thin reading for Brisk-S with high reasoning and retry. Its ambiguous-entity pass is 97.6%, 0.6 points over, with a 29.9% wrong-side chance under the traffic-share what-if. Its date-math pass is 97.9% (16.5%). Ambiguous entities are its leg of the routed mix, and the looser-budget fallback needs all four tasks to hold. Fix: name the ambiguous-entity clearance in c-nearest and Watch, and extend next step 2's re-run to ambiguous entities (5,108 cases on the same what-if).

The headline says 'only the two with high reasoning and retry hold 97% in every task'. There are three configurations with high reasoning and retry; the Nano-XS one is at 93.5% on multi-hop. Say 'only two configurations, Atlas-M and Brisk-S with high reasoning and retry, hold 97% in every task', as c-gates does.

The Options table's 'Pass rate' column is overall pass rate. On the first screen it shows six configurations at 97% or more, including Brisk-S with low reasoning and retry at 97.1% and Atlas-M with low reasoning and retry at 97.9%. Both miss the gate on multi-hop, and the page leaves overall pass rate out because 'overall figures would mislead'. Label the column 'overall pass rate (gate reads each task)', or show each configuration's lowest task rate instead.

In 'What you could change', the pass-rate row says lowering the gate admits Brisk-S with low reasoning and retry 'once it reaches 95.6%'. That reads as if the configuration must reach 95.6%. Say 'once the gate is lowered to 95.6%'.

items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline, lede and decision block give the call: no configuration is shown to pass both gates, so ship none as declared. The headline now names the two pass-rate passers correctly, Atlas-M and Brisk-S with high reasoning and retry, which resolves my earlier headline finding. It says why: both are over the 600 ms budget on tail latency over all cases, 870 ms and 2551 ms. It names the main risk, Brisk-S with low reasoning and retry missing multi-hop by 1.4 points, and the way out, per-task latency for a routed mix. The first claim, c-gates, shows the per-task heatmap behind the call. The Options table still heads its column 'Pass rate', with Brisk-S low reasoning and retry at 97.1% and Atlas-M low reasoning and retry at 97.9%. Method now labels it as overall pass rate, and the headline's 'in every task' wording guards the reading, so my earlier label finding is mostly answered.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: I checked each sentence against its block, row by row. c-gates: only Atlas-M and Brisk-S with high reasoning and retry clear 97% in all four tasks, at 97.9% and 97.3% on multi-hop, and multi-hop is the lowest row in every column. c-latency: 870 ms and 2551 ms against 600 ms, matching the range bars. options_dominance flags the same 'at least one task misses' fact as an inference. c-nearest: 95.6% and 96.4% are misses of 1.4 and 0.6 points, and 97.3% and 97.6% clear by 0.3 and 0.6, all matching the dot rows. c-cost: 3.477/0.633 is 5.5 times as much, and the $11,376 monthly gap is right at 4,000,000 calls. 'What we know despite it' is now qualified as 'on today's readings… a miss not yet settled', which resolves my earlier must_fix. The 'What you could change' row now says 'once the gate is lowered to 95.6%', which resolves that should_fix.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: Nothing is recommended. The fallback lean is kept conditional and logged in omitted. The thin readings are visible. c-nearest and Watch now name Brisk-S high reasoning and retry's ambiguous-entity clearance (0.6 points, wrong-side chance 29.9%) next to the multi-hop one (0.3 points, 37.4%). Watch carries low reasoning's 11.9% and 33.3% wrong-side chances and its date math exactly on the line. The confidence caveat on case counts now says low reasoning becomes a candidate only if both misses flip and date math holds, which resolves my earlier must_fix. settle_cases on both Brisk-S configurations with retry reproduces every percentage printed.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: Nothing omitted would change the call. Atlas-M's other thin misses (high reasoning without retry at 96.6% on multi-hop) and Brisk-S high reasoning without retry are over the budget over all cases, so settling them yields no passer. Nano-XS clears no task. A routed mix has no figure, and price_tradeoff confirms there is nothing to price. Calls per task and median latency bear on no gate.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: All four caveats are carried in. Missing per-task counts show up as wrong-side odds under a labelled traffic-share what-if and as sized re-runs. Latency recorded only over all cases is bounded by the partition argument and turned into next step 1. Best-of-eighteen is tied to the thin Brisk-S clearances. No control is scoped to comparisons the call doesn't make.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each step names an experiment or a declaration and what it settles: per-task tail latency for the routed mix; re-runs sized at 22,911 and 5,108 cases for high reasoning, and 1,685 and 7,567 for low reasoning, matching the tool's 80% two-sided sizes; the date-math line that no run can settle; and the owner's declaration of which gate gives way. items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: Each block draws its claim's figures. The c-gates heatmap outlines the cells under the gate. The c-latency range bars mark the 600 ms budget. The c-nearest dots sit against the 97% line with no interval drawn, which the caption explains. The c-cost bars include the nearest miss inside the budget for scale. The c-fail cards match the snapshot's three kept examples, and the caption says they are a sample. Flipping any of these values would force its claim to change.

findings.finding: Next step 4 ('Improve multi-hop planning… where the kept failure merges hops into one search') rests on one kept card, TQ-0418. The snapshot doesn't say how many multi-hop failures there were for Brisk-S with low reasoning and retry, so hop-collapse may not be the main pattern. Fix: make step 4 conditional, e.g. first tally that configuration's multi-hop failures by pattern from the traces, then target planning only if hop-collapse dominates. c-fail could say in its sentence, not only its caption, that this is one example.
